# Cross-format parity

msf-character-tools 0.4.0; usd-core 0.26.11; ufbx 0.23.1. Errors are the largest point distance divided by the bounding-box diagonal unless stated otherwise; the tests fail above 1e-5.

## Strict tier

### Synthetic USD scenes

Each scene from `tests/public/make_source_fixtures.py` is read as USDA, USDC and USDZ and compared with usd-core (world points at every authored time, `BakeSkinning` for skinned meshes). The FBX twin is the same scene written by the test FBX writer from msf-character-tools' reading of the USD and read back through the FBX adapter. That column is a consistency check (msf writer to msf reader), not an independent reference: it shows the two readers agree on what was carried over, and it does not re-test the USD losses.

### FBX behaviour with no USD counterpart

Pivots, offsets, pre- and post-rotation and the three inherit types are checked against an independent FBX SDK transform formula and the archived affine witness points (`tests/public/test_source_fbx.py`). glTF and USD cannot express them, so there is nothing to compare across formats.

## Exporter tier

Blender FBX twins of the Khronos assets (decision D4) have not been made yet.

### Two exports of one model: Kenney's character as FBX and as GLB

`character-female-a` from Kenney's Mini Characters pack (CC0), exported by Kenney as FBX (Autodesk FBX SDK) and as GLB, read through the FBX and glTF paths. Distances are divided by the bounding-box diagonal; the tests allow 1e-3. The exports key the walk clip differently, so they agree closely at shared keys and less between them.

| Pose | FBX vertices | GLB vertices | Largest distance to the other export |
|---|---|---|---|
| rest | 553 | 1576 | 5.9e-09 |
| walk 0.1 s | 553 | 1576 | 2.6e-07 |
| walk 0.25 s | 553 | 1576 | 5.6e-04 |
| walk 0.5 s | 553 | 1576 | 3.1e-08 |

### DCC reference frames from the ufbx corpus

The OBJ frames that each DCC exported alongside the ufbx corpus files, compared with msf-character-tools' world points (`tests/internal/test_source_fbx_dcc.py`), with the axes and unit read from each file's own header. "explained" rows differ only on meshes that carry a declared loss that changes points; "refused" rows are singular transforms; "skipped" rows are OBJ files in skin bind space, frames ufbx evaluates without extrapolation, files with only skipped surface kinds, and skinned meshes at rest whose rest pose differs from the bind pose.
